# Jeremiah 12 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA (Council Arbiter) | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Source Manuscript:** Leningrad Codex (B19A)

---

**1** Righteous are You, O LORD, when I plead my case before You; yet I would speak with You about Your justice: Why does the way of the wicked prosper? Why do all who are treacherous thrive?

**2** You plant them, and they take root; they grow and produce fruit. You are near in their mouths but far from their hearts.

**3** But You, O LORD, know me; You see me, and test my heart toward You. Pull them out like sheep for the slaughter, and set them apart for the day of slaughter.

**4** How long will the land mourn and the grass of every field wither? For the evil of those who dwell in it the beasts and the birds are swept away, because they said, "He will not see our end."

**5** "If you have raced with men on foot, and they have wearied you, how will you compete with horses? And if in a safe land you are so trusting, what will you do in the thicket of the Jordan?

**6** For even your brothers and the house of your father, even they have dealt treacherously with you; they are in full cry after you. Do not believe them, though they speak friendly words to you."

**7** "I have forsaken My house; I have abandoned My heritage; I have given the beloved of My soul into the hands of her enemies.

**8** My heritage has become to Me like a lion in the forest; she has lifted up her voice against Me; therefore I hate her.

**9** Is My heritage to Me like a hyena's lair, with birds of prey circling against her? Go, assemble all the wild beasts; bring them to devour.

**10** Many shepherds have destroyed My vineyard; they have trampled down My portion; they have made My pleasant portion a desolate wilderness.

**11** They have made it a desolation; desolate, it mourns to Me. The whole land is made desolate, but no one lays it to heart.

**12** Upon all the bare heights in the desert destroyers have come, for the sword of the LORD devours from one end of the land to the other; no flesh has peace.

**13** They have sown wheat and have reaped thorns; they have tired themselves out but profit nothing. They shall be ashamed of their harvests because of the fierce anger of the LORD."

**14** Thus says the LORD concerning all My evil neighbors who touch the heritage that I have given My people Israel to inherit: "Behold, I will pluck them up from their land, and I will pluck up the house of Judah from among them.

**15** And after I have plucked them up, I will again have compassion on them, and I will bring them again each to his heritage and each to his land.

**16** And it shall come to pass, if they will diligently learn the ways of My people, to swear by My name, 'As the LORD lives,' even as they taught My people to swear by Baal, then they shall be built up in the midst of My people.

**17** But if any nation will not listen, then I will utterly pluck it up and destroy it, declares the LORD."

---
## SOPHIA's Council Notes

SOPHIA detected **6** significant divergence(s) in Jeremiah 12.

- **12:3** — EMET preserves Hebrew word-order and hyphenated compounds; LOGOS renders into natural English; PNEUMA interprets for contemporary application.

- **12:7** — EMET preserves Hebrew word-order and hyphenated compounds; LOGOS renders into natural English; PNEUMA interprets for contemporary application.

- **12:8** — EMET preserves Hebrew word-order and hyphenated compounds; LOGOS renders into natural English; PNEUMA interprets for contemporary application.

- **12:4** — EMET preserves Hebrew word-order and hyphenated compounds; LOGOS renders into natural English; PNEUMA interprets for contemporary application.

- **12:15** — EMET preserves Hebrew word-order and hyphenated compounds; LOGOS renders into natural English; PNEUMA interprets for contemporary application.

- **12:16** — EMET preserves Hebrew word-order and hyphenated compounds; LOGOS renders into natural English; PNEUMA interprets for contemporary application.

## Translation Notes (Select)

### EMET
- **12:1**: Tzaddiq attah YHWH — 'Righteous are You, YHWH.' Jeremiah's complaint follows the form of a legal proceeding (riv). The prophet acts as plaintiff questioning God's justice.
- **12:5**: The 'thicket of the Jordan' (ge'on ha-Yarden) refers to the dense growth along the riverbanks where lions lurked (cf. 49:19). A metaphor for escalating difficulty.
- **12:9**: Ayit tzavua — possibly 'speckled bird of prey.' The image suggests Israel looks foreign among the nations, attracting hostile attention.

### LOGOS
- **12:1-4**: Jeremiah's second confession. The theodicy question parallels Psalm 73 and Habakkuk 1:13. Unlike Job, Jeremiah receives God's answer immediately — and it's not comforting.
- **12:5**: God's response is one of the most striking in Scripture: instead of answering the complaint, He tells Jeremiah things will get worse. The race against horses is proverbial.
- **12:7-13**: A remarkable passage where God Himself laments. The divine warrior has become the divine mourner, grieving over His own judgment on His own people.

### PNEUMA
- **12:1**: Jeremiah does something incredibly bold — he challenges God's justice to His face. And God doesn't rebuke him for it. The Bible makes room for honest wrestling with God.
- **12:5**: God's answer is basically: 'You think this is hard? It's about to get much worse.' Sometimes God doesn't remove our pain — He builds our capacity to endure it.
- **12:7**: One of the most heartbreaking verses in the Bible — God says He has abandoned the thing He loves most. God's judgment isn't cold or detached; it costs Him deeply.

— SOPHIA
